---
title: "7. Air vs. ground communities"
format:
  html:
    toc: false
---

*Compare arthropod communities from Malaise traps (flying insects) and soil/litter extraction (ground-dwelling invertebrates) using genus-level Bray–Curtis distances.*

Because the two sampling methods target different ecological layers, we expect their communities to differ systematically — regardless of habitat. Here we test that expectation and identify which taxonomic groups drive the difference.

### Bray–Curtis distances on genus composition

We use genus-level normalised counts rather than ASV-level counts. This reduces the effect of sequencing noise and makes the comparison more robust across sampling methods:

```r
bray_dist <- as.matrix(vegdist(t(cladecounts$norm$genus), method = "bray"))
```

### Run PCoA

```r
pcoa_res2 <- pcoa(bray_dist, correction = "cailliez")
```

### Plot PCoA (genus level)

Point shape distinguishes sampling method; point colour shows habitat type as before.

```r
layout(matrix(c(1, 2, 3, 3), 2, 2, byrow = TRUE))
par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 1), xpd = TRUE, cex.axis = 1)

xlab <- paste0("PC1 (", round(pcoa_res2$values$Rel_corr_eig[1] * 100), "%)")
ylab <- paste0("PC2 (", round(pcoa_res2$values$Rel_corr_eig[2] * 100), "%)")

# Panel: Malaise trap
plot(pcoa_res2$vectors[, 1], pcoa_res2$vectors[, 2],
     pch = pch, col = "white", bg = "white",
     xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, main = "Malaise trap")
points(pcoa_res2$vectors[DS_malaise, 1], pcoa_res2$vectors[DS_malaise, 2],
       pch = pch[DS_malaise], col = "black",
       bg  = color_habitat[DS_malaise], cex = 1.4)

# Panel: Soil/litter
plot(pcoa_res2$vectors[, 1], pcoa_res2$vectors[, 2],
     pch = pch, col = "white", bg = "white",
     xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, main = "Soil/litter")
points(pcoa_res2$vectors[DS_soillitter, 1], pcoa_res2$vectors[DS_soillitter, 2],
       pch = pch[DS_soillitter], col = "black",
       bg  = color_habitat[DS_soillitter], cex = 1.4)

# Legend
plot.new()
legend("center", bty = "n",
       legend = names(habitat_cols),
       pt.bg  = habitat_cols,
       pch = 21, pt.cex = 1.6, cex = 1.1,
       title = "Habitat")
```

### Which orders differ between methods?

We plot the mean relative abundance of insect orders in each sampling method to see which taxonomic groups are over-represented in the air vs. the ground layer:

```r
orders <- rownames(cladecounts$norm$order)

mean_malaise    <- rowMeans(cladecounts$norm$order[, DS_malaise,    drop = FALSE])
mean_soillitter <- rowMeans(cladecounts$norm$order[, DS_soillitter, drop = FALSE])

top <- order(pmax(mean_malaise, mean_soillitter), decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 10, 2, 2))
barplot(
  rbind(mean_malaise[top], mean_soillitter[top]),
  beside  = TRUE,
  horiz   = TRUE,
  names.arg = orders[top],
  col     = c("#4895ef", "#d4a017"),
  las     = 1,
  xlab    = "Mean relative abundance",
  main    = "Top orders by sampling method"
)
legend("bottomright", bty = "n",
       legend = c("Malaise trap", "Soil/litter"),
       fill   = c("#4895ef", "#d4a017"))
```
